column1: # `hidden-treasures.md` Section 4's fixed records, which no capture has
# ever shown. Ten of its `Thou dost find` results are in
# corpse!`, `a potion!`, `a ring of keys!`, `a ring!`, `a rotting body!`,
# `a sack of gold!`, `a scroll!`, `a shield!` - and every record in the
# published table sits at one Underworld cell, `(233, 233)`.
# No seed in the suite stands anywhere near it, which is why the whole
# family was unreachable. `seed_position` is what makes it a seed rather
# than a scripted crossing of the underworld:
# Clean-room safe on the same terms as `seed_inventory`: the plane and the
# coordinate come from the command line, not from any asset. Both come from
# Section 2 gates several records on party state - record 13 stages only
# with no keys owned, 15 only with a zero equipment counter, 14 once per
# in-game day - so which of the ten a given search yields is a function of
# the save, and the shipped starting party is the plainest state to ask
# from. The scenario asserts nothing about which one appears; it searches
# and lets the comparator say whether the two sides agree.
# A repeat search is included because Section 2's `One-shot` column says
